summary: Attacked part 1 of the Curves, abelian varieties and Shimura varieties area — AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli, ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights, ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity, PELModuli, ShimuraCompactifications, ShimuraData and ShimuraVarieties: 7 roadmaps, 52 stages, 61 accepted paper routes. One finding, medium: the all-degree de Rham and Hodge cohomology package for abelian schemes, including the exterior-algebra isomorphism, is owned by nothing, while stage A4 explicitly restricts itself to degree one and two routed papers depend on the higher-degree structure. The other heads are clean and unusually well so. Duplication in particular is clean where it was most likely: five of the seven roadmaps cover one subject, and each states in its summary what it does not build, with the cross-references those disclaimers make (V2, V8, H2) verified to resolve and to own what is claimed.
checked: All 52 stages of the seven roadmaps with their descriptions, dependencies and acceptance clauses, and the accepted audit verdict for each: 45 not built, 5 partly built, 2 process.

Eligibility, measured rather than assumed, and one disclosure. Of the papers this session has reviewed, exactly one routes here: PAPER-VANHOFTEN-24 to AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A2, A3 and A4. I reviewed that extraction and did not write it, the target of this job is the area, and the finding below does not rest on it — its two sources are PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23 and PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24. Same standard as the Nakamura disclosure in RT-AREA-algebraicnt-1.

All 61 routes and their reasons, with the stage distribution: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli takes 25 (A4 10, A2 10, A6 8, A3 6), ShimuraCompactifications 8 (C3 5, C5 5), ShimuraData 7, ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity 7, ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights 6, ShimuraVarieties 5, PELModuli 3.

Duplication, the head most likely to yield here and the one I ran hardest, because five of the seven roadmaps cover a single subject: ShimuraData supplies the group-theoretic input, ShimuraVarieties the varieties and canonical models, ShimuraCompactifications the toroidal boundary, PELModuli the moduli description, and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli the abelian-scheme library underneath. No mathematics is planned twice, and the reason is that each summary states its own exclusions: ShimuraData constructs Deligne's category 'without restricting it to PEL, Hodge, or abelian type' and adds that 'A moduli interpretation is a theorem about particular data, not part of this definition'; ShimuraVarieties says 'Neither Deligne's abelian-type reduction nor a PEL moduli construction is a proof for all data'; PELModuli supplies concrete families 'without redefining a general Shimura variety to be a PEL moduli space'; ShimuraCompactifications says 'Minimal characteristic-zero compactifications are already owned by V2 and V8. This roadmap does not reconstruct them.'

The cross-references those disclaimers depend on, verified rather than taken on trust, because a scope boundary that points at a stage which does not own the material is the defect I found in the AdicSpaces link map. All three resolve and are accurate. ShimuraVarieties:V2 is 'Baily-Borel algebraicity and minimal compactification', which constructs them. ShimuraVarieties:V8 is 'The algebraic tower and modular-curve comparison', and although its title does not say so its body does the rest: it instructs the worker to 'descend the minimal compactifications' and to 'Compare minimal compactifications through ModularCurvesPartII R13.4a/R13.4b'. So 'owned by V2 and V8' is exact — V2 constructs, V8 descends and compares. PELModuli's 'The Hilbert-specific arbitrary-prime models have their own owner H2' resolves to HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves:H2, titled 'Integral models at arbitrary p', which is precisely that.

Dependency bookkeeping, the head that produced a finding in part 1 of the Algebraic number theory area. Clean here: all seven roadmaps declare between five and seven prerequisites, and for every one of them the set of roadmaps reached by a cross-roadmap stage `requires` edge is contained in its declared `prerequisites`, so no stage edge is unrecorded.

ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity's empty `consumers`, which is the shape that looked like a finding in the Analytic area and again here. It is correct, and exactly so: the roadmaps that cite ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity number seven — ShimuraVarieties, ShimuraData, NeronModelsAndSemistableAbelianVarieties, ModularCurvesPartII, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations, ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations and AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli — and those are precisely its own seven declared prerequisites, citing it as their consumer. It is a sink, so nothing downstream is missing.

The library boundary, which cannot yield much here and the reason is worth recording: 45 of the 52 stages are audited `not built`, including every stage of ShimuraVarieties (10 of 10) and PELModuli (7 of 7) and all six of ArakelovGeometryAndAbelianHeights. This is frontier material, so there is almost nothing in the libraries for a stage to duplicate — the opposite situation from the Elementary area, where everything was built and the accepted audit carried the mapping. The only stages that are not `not built` are AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A0 (process) and A1 and A3 (partly built), ComplexMultiplicationAndExplicitReciprocity:CM.6 (process), ShimuraCompactifications:C0 and C1, and ShimuraData:D1 — all foundational layers (rigidity, torsion and pairings, admissible fans, the Deligne torus) where partial library support is expected.

Whether the all-degree de Rham package of the finding is owned anywhere under another name, before calling it absent. Searched both roadmap directories for 'Berthelot-Breen-Messing', 'Breen-Messing' and 'BBM' (0 files), for 'higher de Rham' and the Hodge-cohomology-of-an-abelian-scheme phrasings (0), for a wedge or exterior power of H^1 (0), and for 'finite locally free and commute with base change' (0). 'Exterior algebra' matches three files and none is this statement: SpinRepresentations means the Clifford/exterior algebra of a quadratic space, BorelRegulators something else again, and ComplexComparisonPartII:C5 means the exterior algebra of Kahler differentials used to build the de Rham complex ('construct its algebraic de Rham complex from the existing Kahler differential/exterior algebra'), which is the construction of Omega^j and not the theorem that the induced map on cohomology of an abelian scheme is an algebra isomorphism. This distinction is the same class of trap as the three same-name collisions this session (Smyth's two theorems, Salem numbers versus Salem-Spencer sets, and Heath-Brown's identity versus his large sieve), so it was settled by reading the stage rather than counting matches.

Library trees, with their sizes printed beside every result after two wrong paths produced false cleans earlier in this session: a full Mathlib checkout of 8556 .lean files and the Tau Ceti library tree of 5268.

findings.where: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4 (Degree-one realizations and deformation theory), and the atlas as a whole
findings.claim: Nothing plans the all-degree de Rham and Hodge cohomology of an abelian scheme, or the exterior-algebra isomorphism that organises it: for every k, i and j the modules H^k(X, Omega^bullet) and H^i(X, Omega^j) are finite locally free and commute with base change, and the canonical map from the exterior algebra on H^1(X, Omega^bullet) to H^*(X, Omega^bullet) is an isomorphism of algebras (Berthelot-Breen-Messing 2.5.2). A4 constructs relative H^1_dR with its Hodge exact sequence, Gauss-Manin connection, cup product and base change, and then limits itself explicitly — 'These are degree-one statements'. Two routed papers depend on the higher-degree structure, and the two routes disagree about how it should be obtained, which is itself evidence that no stage settles it: one asks for the whole package as 'the natural completion of A4's degree-one statements', the other asks a worker to derive the exterior-algebra computation from A3 to A5 without building a second abelian-variety theory. A worker reading A4 as written would produce neither.
findings.evidence: A4's own text, after listing relative H^1_dR, the Hodge exact sequence, the Gauss-Manin connection, the cup-product pairing and base change: 'These are degree-one statements; invoking the full Hodge or etale comparison theorem as an unnamed dependency is unnecessary.' The first need, PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23 routed to A4: 'A4 constructs the relative H^1_dR of an abelian scheme with its Hodge exact sequence, Gauss-Manin connection, cup product and base change, and says explicitly that these are degree-one statements. The input this paper needs, Berthelot-Breen-Messing 2.5.2, is the whole package: for every k, i and j the modules H^k(X, Omega^bullet_{X/Abar}) and H^i(X, Omega^j_{X/Abar}) are finite locally free and commute with base change, and the canonical map wedge^* H^1(X, Omega^bullet_{X/Abar}) -> H^*(X, Omega^bullet_{X/Abar}) is an isomorphism of algebras. That exterior structure is what makes the prismatic Ext-sheaf of an abelian scheme finite locally free of rank 2 dim(X), and it is the natural completion of A4's degree-one statements.' The second, PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 routed to A3, A4 and A5: 'Reuse multiplication torsors, degree-one realizations and complex uniformization; derive the exterior-algebra computation from those and the existing comparison supplier, not from a second abelian-variety theory.' Ownership searches across both roadmap directories: 'Berthelot-Breen-Messing', 'Breen-Messing' and 'BBM' return 0 files; 'higher de Rham' and the Hodge-cohomology-of-an-abelian-scheme phrasings return 0; a wedge or exterior power of H^1 returns 0; 'finite locally free and commute with base change' returns 0. 'Exterior algebra' returns three files, none of them this statement — SpinRepresentations (the Clifford algebra of a quadratic space), BorelRegulators, and ComplexComparisonPartII:C5, which uses 'the existing Kahler differential/exterior algebra' to construct the algebraic de Rham complex, i.e. the construction of Omega^j rather than a theorem about the cohomology algebra of an abelian scheme.
findings.fix: Name the all-degree package as a target, with Berthelot-Breen-Messing 2.5.2 as its source. The natural owner is A4, as an explicit extension of its degree-one scope rather than a contradiction of it: state that for an abelian scheme over a base, H^k of the de Rham complex and H^i of each Omega^j are finite locally free and commute with base change in every degree, and that the canonical map from the exterior algebra on H^1_dR to H^*_dR is an isomorphism of algebras. A4's self-limiting sentence should then be narrowed to what it was for — that the full Hodge or etale comparison theorem is not invoked as an unnamed dependency — so that it no longer excludes the higher-degree statements the area needs. PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24's route gives the proof strategy to record alongside it, deriving the exterior-algebra computation from the degree-one realizations of A3 to A5 and the existing comparison supplier rather than from a second abelian-variety theory, and PAPER-ANSCHUTZ-LEBRAS-23 is the source that needs the finite local freeness and base change in every degree. If instead the higher-degree material is judged to belong outside this roadmap, the fix is to say where, because at present the two routes point at a stage that disclaims them.
